brief: A caddy that holds two jerry cans of petrol upright in the boot of my car.

requirements.requirement: Caddy structure with two upright bays for jerry cans
requirements.evidence: Build is a 4-cell rectangular tray (334x418mm footprint) with 1-storey walls around the perimeter (pieces at q0,0 1,0 0,1 1,1 levels 0 and 1). Cells provide containment but no dedicated jerry-can fixtures, straps, or dividers were added; check_build meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Holds cans upright and prevents tipping/sliding in car boot
requirements.evidence: No bin inserts, restraints, lids or handles added; low 80mm wall height (~169mm total) cannot reliably restrain tall jerry cans under braking/cornering. Configurator has no jerry-can prop to verify fit.

requirements.requirement: Suitable/safe for petrol transport in vehicle boot
requirements.evidence: No verification of leak-proofing, ventilation, load rating, or chemical resistance. Configurator checks geometry only; parts are 3D-printed in user-chosen material with no food/fuel/dishwasher/heat certification. Cannot claim petrol-safe.

finish.summary: Built a 2x2-cell open-top caddy base with perimeter walls, capped and bolted, mesh clear. It provides a boot-sized tray for two upright positions but lacks tall retention, straps, or fuel-safe certification, so upright secure transport of petrol jerry cans is not demonstrated.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
